text:
Maya: Heads-up — seeing a perf regression on A10 when max_tokens_per_batch was bumped to 32k in the canary pool this morning. p95 jumped and throughput dipped.
Oliver: ugh, thanks. any quick numbers or flamegraphs?
Maya: Short dump from spot-check run: 
```
GPU: A10
config: max_batch_size=64, max_tokens_per_batch=32768, kv_cache_prefetch=on
p50: 22ms/token -> 24ms/token
p95: 45ms/token -> 78ms/token
tail: 220ms spikes when many long seqs coalesce
kernel_launches: +18% (more small kernels)
mem_copies: +12% (KV misses causing memcpy)
```
Rachel: That mem_copies line smells like KV cache eviction thrash — large token budgets let long contexts force many distinct KV pages into cache.
Sam: Can we reproduce with seq-shape mix? what was the batch formation policy?
Maya: Canary used continuous-batcher policy v2: pack by arrival, prefer fullness; queue max-age=40ms. Mix was 60% short (<128), 30% medium (512), 10% long (4k). When long arrivals hit, they monopolize token budget and force multiple small-send kernels.
Jordan: So two levers: (1) max_tokens_per_batch per-GPU, (2) queue priority/age policy to avoid long-request starvation or monopolization.
Oliver: Proposed quick patch: enforce per-device token ceilings + soft priority for short requests. Suggest targets: A100: 131072, H100: 131072, A10: 32768, L4: 16384, T4: 8192. These are conservative; can relax after kernel selector improvements.
Maya: I like per-device ceilings. For A10 specifically, lowering to 24k removed the worst tail in a quick local run.
perf-bot: perf-test: a10-canary-sweep-03 completed: baseline p95 78ms -> 49ms after max_tokens=24576 + short-first policy.
Rachel: Kernel selector note: when tokens-per-batch grows, we start choosing non-fused kernels to fit memory. That increases kernel count and syncs. If we can bias selector to prefer fused-attn for mid-range sequences on A10, we might keep higher budgets.
Sam: Can we also change queue policy to: max-age=30ms, when queued_tokens > 0.8 * device_ceiling, prefer short-first for next 10ms window? That should avoid single long request soaking tokens.
Oliver: Agreed. Also add a safeguard: if KV-cache misses per-request > X, reduce target_tokens_for_request by 25% on subsequent scheduling for that client until cache warms.
Maya: I'll add a small experiment harness: run 12h sweep across GPUs with combinations: {max_tokens: [8k,16k,24k,32k], queue_policy: [old,short-first,soft-priority], kv_backoff: [on,off]}. Command I ran locally:
```
./bin/ci-sweep --gpu A10 --workload mix_v2 --max-tokens 24576 --policy short-first --kv-backoff on --duration 4h
```
Jordan: For telemetry, add counters: queued_tokens_histogram, kv_evictions_per_min, kernel_count_per_infer. Then correlate p95 with kernel_count and evictions.
perf-bot: added metrics: runtime.kernel_count, runtime.kv_evictions, scheduler.queued_tokens. Dashboards updated under Runtime > Device Ceilings.
CI-bot: Scheduled canary run: a10-device-ceiling-patch on canary cluster at 02:00UTC.
Oliver: Action items: (1) Maya push per-device ceiling change + config flags for short-first window (2) Rachel file kernel-selector tuning ticket with A10 fusion priority (3) Sam add KV-backoff heuristic and telemetry (4) Jordan run 12h cross-gpu sweep and post CSVs.
Maya: I'll open PR with patches and a short readme for the sweep. Will tag @Oliver and @Rachel for reviews.
Rachel: If we get consistent p95 wins without regression on H100/A100, we can promote to Dedicated canaries next week.
Maya: Thanks. Will post initial PR link here once ready. :thumbsup:
Oliver: ping if you want me to help with canary rollout automation.
Maya: will do.
perf-bot: note: observed one regression on L4 with short-first policy at extreme load; flagged for investigation.
Maya: noted. leaving this thread open for sweep logs and quick updates.
ci-bot: canary run results will be posted to #eng-runtime after completion.
